question: to the Commission Özlem Demirel (The Left) Subject:

Since 2020, the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA) has been deploying unmanned helicopters (Schiebel Camcopter S100), supplied by Nordic Unmanned, from Cap Gris-Nez in France to measure sulphur and nitrogen oxide emissions from ships in Emission Control Area (ECA) covering the North Sea and English Channel. The drones are operated by the French Directorate-General for Maritime Affairs. They are also used for general coast guard functions. This includes preventing migration to the UK. 1.

What costs were incurred by EMSA and France for the deployment of EMSA’s remotely piloted aircraft systems in the English Channel between 2020 and 2026, broken down by framework contract with Nordic Unmanned and services actually performed, and how many flight hours have been completed by the Schiebel Camcopter S100 drones in each year since 2020?

In each of these years of operation, what proportion or number of flight hours was apportioned to emissions monitoring as opposed to complementary tasks such as maritime security, fisheries surveillance or migration control, and in how many maritime emergencies was the Camcopter100 used in each of these years?

Where is the collected surveillance data streamed to, and to what extent are EMSA, Frontex or France’s neighbouring countries also given access, and in what way are the UK authorities involved in the operational coordination of the missions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.10.2026) The European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA) may provide Remote Piloted Aviation Systems services to Member States for the purposes they define. Flights are multipurpose as laid out by the European coast guard cooperation1: once deployed, the unmanned aerial vehicle can be used for emissions monitoring, general surveillance, search and rescue and fisheries control. Member States have operational and planning control of the unmanned aerial vehicle, as responsible coastal or port State. The EMSA Work Programme sets out the number of deployment days (days that the drone is available on site) as performance indicator. The table below shows statistics for 2020-25 for sulphur oxides emission measurements, while those for 2026 are not yet available. Costs cover EMSA’s specific contracts. EMSA does not hold data on costs incurred by French authorities. The Schiebel Campocter S-100 has been used throughout. Emissions monitoring data is provided to Member States and streamed into the EU port State control reporting tool (THETIS) for dissemination to Port State Control authorities. Access rights are defined in THETIS for authorised users.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/2434 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 on the
European Maritime Safety Agency and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1406/2002 (Text with EEA relevance), article 12.
